skill.name: skill-onboarding
skill.description: Inspect an installed or newly created agent skill and turn its capabilities, prerequisites, and example prompts into a short usage card. Combine related skills that use the same command-line tool into one card.
skill.summary: Create quick-reference cards for individual agent skills and related command-line tools.
skill.author: yuzhang-zhong

security_audit.summary: The Markdown backticks, multilingual examples, and dictionary key references do not show shell substitution, obfuscation, or credential access. The audit found unsafe temporary-file writes and card paths without a containment check. The workflow also encourages automatic probes of other skills without isolation or separate approval.

remediation.issue: Automatic probes can execute untrusted third-party code.
remediation.suggestion: Default to documentation-only review and require approval for the exact probe. Run approved probes with no credentials, no network, and only temporary writable storage.

remediation.issue: Card paths depend on unchecked skill IDs.
remediation.suggestion: Validate IDs as single filenames and enforce containment under the card directory for reads and writes. Reject symlink destinations and use argument arrays for helper calls.

remediation.issue: State and configuration writes use predictable temporary files.
remediation.suggestion: Use an owner-only state directory and securely create a unique temporary file before atomic replacement. Reject symlinked state directories and test concurrent writes.

remediation.issue: The messaging exception conflicts with the read-only boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the small-group exception. Stop at request construction for all external writes, and label those actions as not run.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic probes cross the target skill trust boundary
semantic_findings.description: The workflow can automatically launch another skill's scripts without requiring isolation or approval for the specific command. Even help and dry-run calls execute target code with the agent's available permissions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both versions require real calls and advise retrying without arguments when help fails. Neither makes code review, isolation, or separate user approval a prerequisite.

semantic_findings.title: Small-group messaging exception weakens the read-only boundary

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both language versions contain the conflicting rules. No actual message send or bundled messaging implementation was found.

content.user_title: Create a Quick-Reference Card for an Agent Skill
content.value_statement: Skill documentation can make useful commands and prerequisites hard to find. This skill organizes those details into a short card with example requests and verification status.
actual_capabilities: Reviews skill instructions and reference materials to identify capabilities and prerequisites.
Uses CLI or script probes to check selected features and report setup problems.
Groups skills for the same command-line tool into one card and compares local coverage with the tool's command inventory.
Produces short cards with verification status, grouped capabilities, and reusable example requests.
Tracks completed onboarding locally and supports settings for language, line limits, automatic triggers, and exclusions.
limitations: This skill does not score quality or certify security.
A help or dry-run option does not guarantee that a target script is safe to execute.
Availability depends on the local interpreter, tools, and dependencies.
The bundled inventory checks WorkBuddy and Claude skill directories, so it can miss installations elsewhere.

use_cases.title: Learn a newly installed skill
use_cases.description: Turn the supplied documentation into a list of common tasks, lesser-known options, and sample requests.

use_cases.title: Check onboarding for a new release
use_cases.description: Compare a skill's release documentation with its declared entry points and identify prerequisites to verify before sharing it.

use_cases.title: Combine related CLI skills
use_cases.description: Build one task-based reference from several approved skill documents and a supplied command inventory.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a first-use card
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: learn one skill from its documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use only the skill documentation I provide. List three useful tasks and one example request for each. Do not run commands or save files.

prompt_templates.title: Identify missing prerequisites
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare to use a skill in a new environment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill's prerequisites and the setup notes I provide. Separate confirmed dependencies from items that still need checking. Do not run commands.

prompt_templates.title: Build a shared tool card
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare several skills for one CLI.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these skill documents with the command inventory I provide. Group tasks by user goal and label features without a matching local skill.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a first-run verification
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a review for a skill release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a usage card from this release and my existing test results. List unverified claims and propose isolated checks with fake data. Do not run them.

output: Status: Documented, not verified in this environment.
Extract text and tables or combine pages into a single PDF.
Example request: Tell me which pages are scans before extracting their text.
Prerequisite to check: Text recognition for scans may require a separate system tool.

output_examples.input: Combine the supplied coding assistant skill documents into one card.
output: Status: Based on documentation and the supplied command inventory.
Group tasks into editing, test runs, and project preferences.
Inventory gap: The tool lists background jobs, but none of the supplied skills cover them.
Example request: Summarize the project preferences that affect this change.

best_practices: Start with one named skill or a user-approved set of related skills.
Use documentation and existing test results first, and label untested capabilities.
Approve each live check separately. Use fake data in an isolated environment without credentials or network access.
anti_patterns: Running a newly installed script just because it advertises help or dry-run mode.
Calling a capability verified based only on the documentation.
Using production data or sending real messages to complete a usage card.

faq.question: What does a usage card include?
faq.answer: It includes a verification status, useful tasks, examples, and any prerequisites or limits discovered during review.

faq.question: Can it cover more than one skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It can group related skills for the same tool by task and highlight commands that lack a matching local skill.

faq.question: Does it prove that a skill is safe?
faq.answer: No. A usage card describes capabilities and the results of selected checks. It is not a security audit.

faq.question: What does it store locally?
faq.answer: The workflow archives Markdown cards and uses a Python helper to store onboarding history and preferences under the WorkBuddy onboarding directory.

faq.question: Can I turn off automatic onboarding?
faq.answer: Yes. Disable the automatic trigger and the separate skill-creator pairing setting. Use the exclusion list to skip individual skills.

faq.question: Which card languages are supported?
faq.answer: The default is Chinese. You can choose English or set the card to follow the language of your request.
